original_question: For a statistical manifold, when is the identity map a critical point of the bienergy functional for maps from (M, g, nabla) to (M, g, nabla^*)?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Jun-ichi Inoguchi, item 5, second bullet open problem: "Investigate statistical manifolds whose identity map is a critical point of the bienergy functional." The surrounding paragraph makes clear that the relevant identity map is the self-map considered from the statistical manifold to the same manifold equipped with the conjugate connection ∇*. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct geometric object (the identity map), the correct source/target setup ((M,g,∇) to (M,g,∇*)), and the correct variational notion (criticality for the bienergy rather than mere harmonicity). So it is aimed at the exact second bullet of Section 1, item 5, not the adjacent bullet about parallel K. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper phrases this as an investigation/classification problem for the class of statistical manifolds, not just as an informal "when" question about one fixed manifold. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
It should explicitly name the map as id_M:(M,g,∇)→(M,g,∇*), where ∇* is the affine connection conjugate (dual) to ∇ with respect to g. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The variational statement is local: the bienergy is taken over a relatively compact region Ω⊂M, so criticality should be understood over every such Ω (equivalently, under variations supported in Ω). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

To be fully stand-alone, the bienergy should be defined, e.g. E_2(φ;Ω)=(1/2)∫_Ω |τ(φ)|^2 dν_g, with τ the tension field of the map computed using ∇ on the domain and ∇* on the target; the target paper indicates this setup, and the same statistical bi-energy definition is explicitly written in the later exposition of the same framework. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The motivational context omitted in the draft is that the paper first discusses statistically harmonic maps, notes that the identity map need not be harmonic, and relates its tension to the difference tensor K and to apolarity before posing the bienergy question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

No extra assumptions such as compactness, dimension, curvature, homogeneity, or completeness are imposed in the open problem itself; adding any of these would make the question less paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Let (M,g,∇) be a statistical manifold, and let ∇* be the affine connection conjugate to ∇ with respect to g. Determine the statistical manifolds for which the identity map id_M:(M,g,∇)→(M,g,∇*) is a critical point, for every relatively compact region Ω⊂M, of the bienergy E_2(id_M;Ω)=(1/2)∫_Ω |τ(id_M)|^2 dν_g under variations supported in Ω, where τ(id_M) is the tension field of id_M computed with domain connection ∇ and target connection ∇*. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: The draft is already very close because Section 1, item 5 first introduces harmonic maps from a statistical manifold to an affine manifold, then specializes to statistically harmonic maps by taking the target connection to be the conjugate connection ∇*, observes that the identity map need not be harmonic and links this to apolarity, and finally poses two separate bullets. The second bullet is exactly the bienergy question. So the paper-faithful refinement should preserve the identity map, the conjugate target ∇*, and the local bienergy-over-Ω formulation, while not drifting to the neighboring 'parallel K' problem or importing later curvature assumptions from other work. This paper does not formulate the question as Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the nearest official formulation is the second bullet in Section 1, item 5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
